title: Look up a product by position

title: List the senior patient names
description:
SCENARIO:

A clinic desk wants a quick list of patient names for a senior-care leaflet.

RULES:

- A patient counts as senior when age is 65 or older.

- Return the names of the senior patients only.

- Keep the input order.

- When nobody qualifies, return an empty array.

INPUT:

An array of patient objects: [{ "name": "John", "age": 72 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array of names, for example ["John", "Lisa"].

title: Count the cheap shelf items
description:
SCENARIO:

A shop manager wants to know how many items on a shelf are priced below $10.

RULES:

- Count items whose price is strictly below 10.

- An item priced exactly 10 does not count.

- Return a number.

- An empty shelf counts as 0.

INPUT:

An array of items: [{ "name": "Pen", "price": 2.5 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

A number, for example 2.

title: Show the in-stock product names
description:
SCENARIO:

A warehouse screen lists the products that can be sold right now.

RULES:

- A product is in stock when stock is greater than 0.

- Return the names of in-stock products in input order.

- Products with stock 0 are out of stock and must be left out.

- Return an empty array when nothing is in stock.

INPUT:

An array of products: [{ "name": "A", "stock": 5 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array of names, for example ["A", "C"].

title: Add up the article reading time
description:
SCENARIO:

A blog editor wants the total minutes needed to read a set of articles.

RULES:

- Sum the minutes of every article.

- Return a number.

- An empty list returns 0.

INPUT:

An array of articles: [{ "title": "Intro", "minutes": 3 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

A number, for example 8.

title: Pick the discount-eligible customers
description:
SCENARIO:

A store gives a discount to senior citizens and to GOLD members.

RULES:

- A customer is eligible when age is 65 or older OR membership is "GOLD".

- Return the names of eligible customers in input order.

- Return an empty array when nobody qualifies.

INPUT:

An array of customers: [{ "name": "Jo", "age": 70, "membership": "STD" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array of names.

title: Count the big northern orders
description:
SCENARIO:

A distributor tracks large orders that ship to its northern region.

RULES:

- An order is big when total is 1000 or more.

- Count big orders whose region is "NORTH".

- Orders from other regions never count, however large.

- Return a number; 0 when there are no orders.

INPUT:

An array of orders: [{ "id": 1, "total": 1200, "region": "NORTH" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

A number, for example 2.

title: Compute the net pay records
description:
SCENARIO:

A payroll clerk checks which employees have a valid net paycheck.

RULES:

- net = base + bonus - deduction.

- Return an array of { "name", "net" } objects for employees whose net is 0 or more.

- Skip employees whose net is negative (invalid rows).

- Keep the input order and use exactly the keys name and net.

INPUT:

An array of employees: [{ "name": "Ana", "base": 1000, "bonus": 100, "deduction": 50 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array like [{ "name": "Ana", "net": 1050 }].

title: Total the unpaid invoice amounts
description:
SCENARIO:

A bookkeeper wants the money still outstanding.

RULES:

- Sum the amount of every invoice where paid is false.

- Invoices already paid are ignored.

- Return a number; 0 when nothing is unpaid.

INPUT:

An array of invoices: [{ "id": 1, "amount": 600, "paid": false }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

A number, for example 900.

title: Count the account statuses
description:
SCENARIO:

An admin page shows how many rows are in each account status.

RULES:

- Count rows with status "ACTIVE", "INACTIVE" and "BANNED".

- Rows with any other status are ignored.

- Return an object with exactly the keys active, inactive and banned.

- Every count starts at 0.

INPUT:

An array of rows: [{ "status": "ACTIVE" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

{ "active": 2, "inactive": 1, "banned": 1 }

title: Classify the student results
description:
SCENARIO:

A teacher needs a pass/fail label for every student submission.

RULES:

- score 60 or higher is "PASS", below 60 is "FAIL".

- A score outside 0..100, or not a number, is "INVALID".

- Return an array of { "name", "result" } objects in input order.

- An empty class returns an empty array.

INPUT:

An array of students: [{ "name": "Ana", "score": 75 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array like [{ "name": "Ana", "result": "PASS" }].

title: Summarise the stock list
description:
SCENARIO:

A shop owner wants one object summarising the whole stock list.

RULES:

- totalQty is the sum of every qty.

- totalValue is the sum of qty * price for every item.

- cheapest is the name of the item with the lowest price; when prices tie, keep the first item in the input.

- An empty list returns { "totalQty": 0, "totalValue": 0, "cheapest": null }.

INPUT:

An array of items: [{ "name": "A", "qty": 5, "price": 2 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

{ "totalQty": 10, "totalValue": 32, "cheapest": "A" }

title: Rename the raw user fields
description:
SCENARIO:

An import file uses long field names; the app wants short ones.

RULES:

- Map user_id to id, full_name to name and signup_year to year.

- Values are copied exactly as they are - no conversion.

- Keep the input order.

- Every returned object has exactly the keys id, name and year.

INPUT:

An array of raw rows: [{ "user_id": 7, "full_name": "Ada", "signup_year": 2021 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array like [{ "id": 7, "name": "Ada", "year": 2021 }].

title: Count the appointment outcomes
description:
SCENARIO:

A clinic dashboard counts appointment outcomes for the front desk.

RULES:

- Count statuses "COMPLETED", "NO_SHOW", "CANCELLED" and "BOOKED".

- Any other status is ignored.

- Return an object with exactly the keys completed, noShow, cancelled and booked.

- Every count starts at 0.

INPUT:

An array of appointments: [{ "patient": "Anna", "status": "COMPLETED" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

{ "completed": 1, "noShow": 1, "cancelled": 1, "booked": 1 }

title: Estimate the return times
description:
SCENARIO:

A waiting-room screen shows when each patient will be called back.

RULES:

- Patients aged 65 or older wait 10 minutes; everyone else waits 5 minutes.

- Return [{ "name", "minutes" }] in queue order.

- An empty queue returns an empty array.

INPUT:

An array of queue entries: [{ "name": "Sara", "age": 70, "arrivedAt": "09:00" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array like [{ "name": "Sara", "minutes": 10 }].

title: Count the October bookings
description:
SCENARIO:

A front desk wants the number of appointments booked during October 2026.

RULES:

- Count appointments with status "BOOKED" whose date falls in October 2026,

  from "2026-10-01" up to and including "2026-10-31" (dates are "YYYY-MM-DD" strings).

- Cancelled or other statuses never count, whatever the date.

- Return a number; 0 when nothing qualifies.

INPUT:

An array of appointments: [{ "id": 1, "patient": "A", "status": "BOOKED", "date": "2026-10-05" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

A number, for example 1.

title: Summarise the billing session
description:
SCENARIO:

A billing clerk wants two numbers from the day's service log.

RULES:

- billed is the sum of minutes * rate for every service.

- longest is the patient name with the largest minutes; ties keep the first patient in the input.

- An empty log returns { "billed": 0, "longest": null }.

INPUT:

An array of services: [{ "patient": "Ana", "minutes": 30, "rate": 10 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

{ "billed": 1200, "longest": "Bo" }

title: Find the process with the worst reject rate
description:
SCENARIO:

A plant supervisor wants the process producing the most rejects.

RULES:

- reject rate = ng / produced (as a percentage).

- Return the name of the process with the highest rate.

- Ties keep the first process in the input.

- Records with produced 0 are broken sensors and must be ignored.

- When every record is ignored, return null.

INPUT:

An array of processes: [{ "process": "P1", "produced": 1000, "ng": 15 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

A process name, for example "P2".

title: Find the shift with the most good units
description:
SCENARIO:

A production board shows which shift made the most good units.

RULES:

- Return the shift name with the highest good value.

- Ties keep the first shift in the input.

- Records where good is greater than produced are invalid and must be ignored.

- When no valid record remains, return null.

INPUT:

An array of shifts: [{ "shift": "S1", "produced": 100, "good": 95 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

A shift name, for example "S2".

title: List the days that hit the target
description:
SCENARIO:

A daily board marks every day that reached its production target.

RULES:

- A day qualifies when produced is greater than or equal to target.

- Return the day names in input order.

- Return an empty array when no day qualifies.

INPUT:

An array of days: [{ "day": "Mon", "produced": 120, "target": 100 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array of day names, for example ["Mon", "Wed"].

title: Find the line with the most wasted material
description:
SCENARIO:

A factory manager wants to know which line wasted the most money in scrap.

RULES:

- waste = defects * unitCost for a line.

- Return the waste of the line with the highest waste (a number).

- Lines with produced 0 are ignored.

- Ties keep the first line in the input.

- When no line remains, return null.

INPUT:

An array of lines: [{ "line": "L1", "produced": 100, "defects": 5, "unitCost": 10 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

A number, for example 50.

title: List the items that need reordering
description:
SCENARIO:

A stockroom prints a reorder sheet each morning.

RULES:

- An item needs reorder when stock is strictly below minLevel.

- Return the names in input order.

- An item exactly at minLevel is fine and must be left out.

- Return an empty array when nothing is low.

INPUT:

An array of items: [{ "name": "A", "stock": 3, "minLevel": 5 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array of names, for example ["A"].

title: Total the stock value
description:
SCENARIO:

A warehouse manager wants the value of all sellable stock.

RULES:

- value = sum of qty * unitPrice for items with qty greater than 0.

- Items with qty 0 or a negative qty (bad rows) are skipped.

- Return a number; 0 when nothing counts.

INPUT:

An array of items: [{ "name": "A", "qty": 2, "unitPrice": 10 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

A number, for example 50.

title: Match the orders against the warehouse stock
description:
SCENARIO:

A warehouse checks which customer orders can be filled today.

RULES:

- For every order, look up the stock of its item in the inventory list.

- An order can be filled when the available stock is at least the ordered qty.

- Return { "id", "available" } for fillable orders only, in input order.

- An item missing from the inventory list counts as available 0.

- An empty order list returns an empty array.

INPUT:

orders: [{ "id": 10, "item": "Pen", "qty": 5 }, ...]
inventory: [{ "item": "Pen", "stock": 7 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array like [{ "id": 10, "available": 7 }].

title: Count the valid submissions
description:
SCENARIO:

A form endpoint receives rows that must be checked before saving.

RULES:

- A row is valid when name (trimmed) is not empty and email contains "@".

- A missing value arrives as an empty string.

- Return the number of valid rows.

INPUT:

An array of rows: [{ "name": "A", "email": "a@x" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

A number, for example 1.

title: Find the duplicate submission codes
description:
SCENARIO:

An intake system flags rows that were submitted twice.

RULES:

- A code is a duplicate when it appears more than once.

- List each duplicate code once, in order of its first repeat occurrence.

- Return an empty array when there are no duplicates.

INPUT:

An array of rows: [{ "code": "A" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array of codes, for example ["A", "B"].

title: Sort the shipments into accepted and rejected
description:
SCENARIO:

A depot splits incoming shipments into accepted and rejected lists.

RULES:

- A shipment is accepted when weight is greater than 0 AND weight is at most 20 AND destination is not empty.

- Anything else is rejected.

- Keep the input order inside each list.

- Return an object with exactly the keys accepted and rejected, each an array of ids.

INPUT:

An array of shipments: [{ "id": 1, "weight": 5, "destination": "NY" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

{ "accepted": [1, 5], "rejected": [2, 3, 4] }

title: Process the order queue against the stock
description:
SCENARIO:

An online shop drains its order queue in one pass, checking each order

against the current stock before marking it.

RULES:

- An order is accepted when every item's available stock covers the requested qty.

- If any item is short, the whole order goes to short.

- An order with no items is accepted (nothing to pick).

- Return { "accepted": [...ids], "short": [...ids] } in input order.

INPUT:

orders: [{ "id": 1, "customer": "Ana", "items": [{ "sku": "P", "qty": 2 }] }, ...]
stock: [{ "sku": "P", "available": 3 }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

{ "accepted": [1], "short": [2, 3] }

title: Pick the next patients to call
description:
SCENARIO:

A clinic receptionist calls urgent waiting patients first.

RULES:

- Only patients with status "WAITING" can be called.

- A waiting patient is urgent when priority is "HIGH" or age is 65 or older.

- Patients with status "LEFT" are never called, even when urgent.

- Return the names in queue order; an empty queue returns [].

INPUT:

An array of patients: [{ "name": "J", "age": 72, "priority": "HIGH", "status": "WAITING" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

An array of names, for example ["J", "L"].

title: Build the daily sales report
description:
SCENARIO:

At closing time a shop needs one object: total sales for the day and a

breakdown by product category.

RULES:

- Only sales whose day is "2026-10-05" are included.

- total is the sum of those amounts.

- byCategory groups the same amounts by the product category from the products list.

- A product missing from the products list belongs to category "UNKNOWN".

- With no sales that day, byCategory is still returned as {}.

INPUT:

sales: [{ "id": 1, "product": "Pen", "amount": 50, "day": "2026-10-05" }, ...]
products: [{ "name": "Pen", "category": "Office" }, ...]

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

{ "total": 80, "byCategory": { "Office": 70, "UNKNOWN": 10 } }

title: Build the shift summary for the board
description:
SCENARIO:

A factory board shows one summary object for a whole production run.

RULES:

- totalProduced, totalGood and totalNg are sums over every shift (ng = produced - good).

- ngRate is totalNg / totalProduced * 100 rounded to 1 decimal place; it is 0 when totalProduced is 0.

- bestShift is the shift with the highest good (ties keep the first); an empty list gives null.

- targetMet is totalProduced >= overallTarget.

- Return an object with exactly the keys totalProduced, totalGood, totalNg, ngRate, bestShift and targetMet.

INPUT:

shifts: [{ "shift": "S1", "produced": 800, "good": 780 }, ...]
overallTarget: a number, for example 2000

EXPECTED OUTPUT:

{ "totalProduced": 2000, "totalGood": 1950, "totalNg": 50, "ngRate": 2.5, "bestShift": "S2", "targetMet": true }
